name: Brain Scan (VST3)
description: A free Windows VST3 synth that stores no waveforms. A specimen is a VOLUME - a scalar field filling a cube, exactly the kind of number a scanner records - and a scan line is a curve through it: one cycle of the sound is the field read along that curve. Bend the curve and the timbre changes because the curve is now somewhere else in the body; a closed loop has no edge and sounds soft, an open segment jumps once per cycle and sounds bright, a corner is a kink at a fixed phase, WARP reads the same shape unevenly. The filter's cutoff and the modulator are the same mechanism read slower - two more curves - and one SCAN control blends the GEOMETRY of two anchor lines before anything is read, so halfway between two sounds is tissue neither of them has visited. Twelve specimens, 128 texels across: seven fields built to give ordinary useful waveforms, three made of edges and spikes, a hollow shell and a simulated brain with skull, cortical folds, a fissure and ventricles. Lines are drawn on a tomography slice that you drive through the body, and watched in a ray-marched gantry where they glow inside the tissue until the density closes over them. IMPORT reads a real volume off disk and uses it instead of the twelve - a NIfTI file, a folder of DICOM slices or a stack of images - resampled in millimetres so an anisotropic scan is not squashed, area-averaged so decimation does not alias, and windowed by percentile so one surgical clip cannot crush the tissue; with a CT loaded, WINDOW and LEVEL are literally a radiographer's window width and level in Hounsfield units. The read has its own controls - GRAIN picks the kernel, smoothed or texel by texel; CONTRAST is a CT window applied to the sound, saturating the read toward a square; FOLD folds it back past the edges - all anti-aliased. The Brokild World FX rack and five macros. Every claim measured: two benches, 115 checks.
note: Windows VST3 - build 260904.3 - free download - 12 specimens at 128 texels plus your own volume (NIfTI, DICOM or an image stack) - hints on every control - 23-page manual.
